title: Enriched right adjoints of simplicial Quillen equivalences
statement:
Use simplicial model categories and cofibrant and fibrant objects of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and simplicial categories and Dwyer--Kan equivalences in the sense of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ be simplicial model categories, in fixed universes enlarged when necessary, and suppose that every object of $\mathcal M$ is cofibrant. Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be an adjunction of underlying ordinary categories, with $L$ preserving cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Assume that $R$ has a simplicial functor structure inducing its given underlying ordinary functor. No enriched adjunction or simplicial structure on $L$ is assumed. Suppose that this ordinary adjunction is a Quillen equivalence: for cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $Y$, a map $LX\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to RY$ is a weak equivalence.

Then $R$ carries cofibrant fibrant objects of $\mathcal N$ to cofibrant fibrant objects of $\mathcal M$, and its simplicial restriction
$$R:\mathcal N^{cf}\longrightarrow\mathcal M^{cf}$$
is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence: its maps on all mapping simplicial sets are weak homotopy equivalences, and its functor on categories of path components is an equivalence. The superscript $cf$ denotes the full simplicial subcategory on the cofibrant fibrant objects. The conclusion concerns the given enrichment of $R$.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], the ordinary adjunction is a Quillen adjunction, $R$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations, and $R$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrant objects. A right adjoint preserves the terminal object, so a fibrant $Y$ has fibrant $RY$. Every object of $\mathcal M$ is cofibrant, hence $RY$ is also cofibrant. Thus the given simplicial functor restricts to $R:\mathcal N^{cf}\to\mathcal M^{cf}$ and its underlying ordinary restriction preserves weak equivalences. Both simplicial categories are locally Kan: apply the mapping-space axiom in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to the initial map of a cofibrant object and the terminal map of a fibrant object.

proof.text: Take the derived adjunction $\mathbf LL\dashv\mathbf RR$ of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. For any $X\in\mathcal M$, choose a fibrant replacement $t:LX\to T(LX)$. Since $X$ is cofibrant and $T(LX)$ is fibrant, the assumed Quillen-equivalence criterion makes its adjoint $X\to R T(LX)$ a weak equivalence. This represents the derived unit. For a fibrant $Y\in\mathcal N$, $RY$ is cofibrant, so the same criterion applied to the identity of $RY$ makes the ordinary counit $LRY\to Y$ a weak equivalence. This represents the derived counit at $Y$. The cited replacement formulas and natural unit/counit construction show that these are the components of the actual coherent derived transformations. Every object of $\mathcal N_\infty$ has a fibrant representative, so both transformations are objectwise equivalences. They exhibit $\mathbf LL$ and $\mathbf RR$ as inverse equivalences. This is a direct use of the stated mapping criterion, not a new Quillen-equivalence lemma.

proof.text: For $\mathcal A=\mathcal M,\mathcal N$, let $B_{\mathcal A}$ be the underlying ordinary category of $\mathcal A^{cf}$, let $i_{\mathcal A}:B_{\mathcal A}\to\mathcal A$ be inclusion, and put $C_{\mathcal A}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A^{cf})$. There is a canonical map $j_{\mathcal A}:N(B_{\mathcal A})\to C_{\mathcal A}$: a string of ordinary arrows is sent to the coherent simplex whose mapping maps are constant at the composites of that string. Equivalently, include the discrete enrichment of $B_{\mathcal A}$ in $\mathcal A^{cf}$ and apply the coherent nerve. The ordinary-nerve identification of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] gives this description. The bifibrant comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] gives an equivalence $e_{\mathcal A}:C_{\mathcal A}\simeq\mathcal A_\infty$ with $e_{\mathcal A}j_{\mathcal A}\simeq q_{\mathcal A}N(i_{\mathcal A})$: the functor $e_{\mathcal A}$ is the inverse equivalence in that cited statement, and agrees with inclusion followed by localization on bifibrants, with its natural, composition-compatible mapping comparison. This is a comparison of functors, including their coherent compositions. The inclusion also gives $N(B_{\mathcal A})[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal A_\infty$. Consequently $j_{\mathcal A}$ itself presents localization of $N(B_{\mathcal A})$ at its weak equivalences: compose with $e_{\mathcal A}$ and use the full functor-category universal property in the cited localization statement.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded foundation; canonical ordinary-nerve to coherent-nerve localization comparisons

proof.text: Put $H=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R|_{\mathcal N^{cf}}):C_{\mathcal N}\to C_{\mathcal M}$ and write $R_0:B_{\mathcal N}\to B_{\mathcal M}$ for the underlying ordinary restriction. The construction of $j$ gives the strict equality $Hj_{\mathcal N}=j_{\mathcal M}N(R_0)$: on each string of arrows both sides are constant at the same composites because the given enrichment of $R$ preserves ordinary arrows and enriched composition. Thus $e_{\mathcal M}Hj_{\mathcal N}\simeq q_{\mathcal M}N(i_{\mathcal M}R_0)$. On the other hand $\mathbf RR\,e_{\mathcal N}j_{\mathcal N}\simeq\mathbf RR\,q_{\mathcal N}N(i_{\mathcal N})\simeq q_{\mathcal M}N(Ri_{\mathcal N})$ by the coherent fibrant-replacement formula of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], since every object of $B_{\mathcal N}$ is fibrant. These right sides agree as functors. By step 3 and the full functor-category localization property of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], restriction along $j_{\mathcal N}$ is fully faithful; the displayed natural equivalence therefore lifts to $e_{\mathcal M}H\simeq\mathbf RR\,e_{\mathcal N}$. Both $e$'s and $\mathbf RR$ are equivalences by steps 2 and 3, so $H$ is an equivalence. This establishes the comparison for the actual given enriched functor without imposing any enrichment on $L$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded foundation; naturality through the strict square on ordinary nerves and the localization universal property

proof.text: For $X,Y\in\mathcal N^{cf}$, [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] supplies the natural mapping-space equivalences $\mathcal N(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{C_{\mathcal N}}(X,Y)$ and $\mathcal M(RX,RY)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{C_{\mathcal M}}(RX,RY)$. Their naturality for simplicial functors makes the square with the given mapping map of $R$ and the mapping-space map of $H$ commute up to the specified homotopy. Since $H$ is an equivalence, its mapping-space maps are equivalences, and two-out-of-three gives that the mapping simplicial-set maps of $R$ are weak homotopy equivalences. On path components these comparisons identify $\pi_0(\mathcal A^{cf})$ with the homotopy category of $C_{\mathcal A}$, preserving composition. The inverse equivalence of $H$ induces an inverse equivalence of these homotopy categories, so the actual functor $\pi_0R$ is an equivalence as well. These are precisely the two clauses of the Dwyer--Kan definition in the cited node.

split_report.summary: Replaced the preliminary attempt with a five-step proof using three existing nodes and no new nodes. The canonical ordinary-nerve to coherent-nerve maps are localization maps; their strictly commuting square for the given simplicial R identifies its coherent nerve with the derived right functor by the full functor-category universal property. Naturality of the coherent-nerve mapping comparison then proves both Dwyer–Kan clauses. Statement unchanged.
